name: Free Verse
description: Poetry without regular meter, rhyme, or other traditional patterns. Relies on natural speech rhythms and line breaks for effect.

name: Haiku
description: Traditional Japanese form with three lines of 5, 7, and 5 syllables. Often captures a moment in nature with seasonal reference (kigo).
templateContent:
Line 1 (5 syllables)
Line 2 (7 syllables)
Line 3 (5 syllables)

name: Tanka
description: Japanese form extending the haiku with two additional 7-syllable lines. Often explores emotional or reflective themes.
templateContent:
Line 1 (5 syllables)
Line 2 (7 syllables)
Line 3 (5 syllables)
Line 4 (7 syllables)
Line 5 (7 syllables)

name: Sonnet (Shakespearean)
description: English sonnet with three quatrains and a couplet. Each line in iambic pentameter (10 syllables, unstressed-stressed pattern).
templateContent:
Line 1 (A rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 2 (B rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 3 (A rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 4 (B rhyme) - iambic pentameter

Line 5 (C rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 6 (D rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 7 (C rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 8 (D rhyme) - iambic pentameter

Line 9 (E rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 10 (F rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 11 (E rhyme) - iambic pentameter
Line 12 (F rhyme) - iambic pentameter

Line 13 (G rhyme) - couplet
Line 14 (G rhyme) - couplet

name: Sonnet (Petrarchan)
description: Italian sonnet with an octave (8 lines) presenting a problem and a sestet (6 lines) offering resolution. Strict ABBAABBA octave rhyme.
templateContent:
Line 1 (A rhyme) - octave begins
Line 2 (B rhyme)
Line 3 (B rhyme)
Line 4 (A rhyme)
Line 5 (A rhyme)
Line 6 (B rhyme)
Line 7 (B rhyme)
Line 8 (A rhyme) - octave ends

Line 9 (C rhyme) - sestet begins (volta/turn)
Line 10 (D rhyme)
Line 11 (E rhyme)
Line 12 (C rhyme)
Line 13 (D rhyme)
Line 14 (E rhyme) - sestet ends

name: Limerick
description: Humorous five-line poem with AABBA rhyme scheme. Lines 1, 2, 5 have 7-10 syllables; lines 3, 4 have 5-7 syllables. Anapestic meter (unstressed-unstressed-stressed).
templateContent:
Line 1 (A rhyme) - 7-10 syllables
Line 2 (A rhyme) - 7-10 syllables
Line 3 (B rhyme) - 5-7 syllables
Line 4 (B rhyme) - 5-7 syllables
Line 5 (A rhyme) - 7-10 syllables, punchline

name: Villanelle
rhymeScheme: ABA ABA ABA ABA ABA ABAA
description: Highly structured 19-line form with two repeating refrains (A1 and A2) and two rhymes throughout. Five tercets and a final quatrain.
templateContent:
A1 - First refrain line
Line 2 (B rhyme)
A2 - Second refrain line

Line 4 (A rhyme)
Line 5 (B rhyme)
A1 - First refrain repeats

Line 7 (A rhyme)
Line 8 (B rhyme)
A2 - Second refrain repeats

Line 10 (A rhyme)
Line 11 (B rhyme)
A1 - First refrain repeats

Line 13 (A rhyme)
Line 14 (B rhyme)
A2 - Second refrain repeats

Line 16 (A rhyme)
Line 17 (B rhyme)
A1 - First refrain
A2 - Second refrain (final quatrain)

name: Ghazal
description: Arabic/Persian form of 5-15 couplets. Each couplet is self-contained. Both lines of first couplet end with refrain (radif); second line of each subsequent couplet ends with same refrain.
templateContent:
Line 1 ending with refrain word/phrase
Line 2 ending with same refrain

Line 3 (different content)
Line 4 ending with refrain

Line 5 (different content)
Line 6 ending with refrain

Line 7 (different content)
Line 8 ending with refrain

Line 9 (different content)
Line 10 ending with refrain - poet's signature (takhallus) often appears here

name: Blank Verse
description: Unrhymed poetry in iambic pentameter. The form of Shakespeare's plays and Milton's Paradise Lost. No set length.
templateContent:
Line 1 - iambic pentameter (10 syllables, da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM)
Line 2 - iambic pentameter
Line 3 - iambic pentameter
...
(continue as needed, no rhyme required)

name: Custom
description: Define your own poetry form with custom requirements. Use the notes section to document your form's structure.

name: Cinquain
description: American form inspired by haiku. Five lines with syllable pattern 2-4-6-8-2, creating a diamond shape. Often focuses on a single image or theme.
templateContent:
Line 1 (2 syllables) - title or subject
Line 2 (4 syllables) - description
Line 3 (6 syllables) - action
Line 4 (8 syllables) - feeling or effect
Line 5 (2 syllables) - synonym or summary

name: Sestina
description: Complex form with six 6-line stanzas and a 3-line envoi. Six end-words rotate through a fixed pattern. The same six words end lines throughout.
templateContent:
Stanza 1: Lines end with words A, B, C, D, E, F
Stanza 2: Lines end with words F, A, E, B, D, C
Stanza 3: Lines end with words C, F, D, A, B, E
Stanza 4: Lines end with words E, C, B, F, A, D
Stanza 5: Lines end with words D, E, A, C, F, B
Stanza 6: Lines end with words B, D, F, E, C, A

Envoi (3 lines): Contains all six words
  Line 1 middle: B, end: E
  Line 2 middle: D, end: C
  Line 3 middle: F, end: A

name: Pantoum
description: Malaysian form with interlocking quatrains. Lines 2 and 4 of each stanza become lines 1 and 3 of the next. In the final stanza, lines 1 and 3 of the first stanza return as lines 4 and 2, creating a circular structure.
templateContent:
Stanza 1:
Line 1 (A) - new
Line 2 (B) - new → becomes line 1 of stanza 2
Line 3 (A) - new
Line 4 (B) - new → becomes line 3 of stanza 2

Stanza 2:
Line 1 (A) - repeat of stanza 1, line 2
Line 2 (B) - new → becomes line 1 of stanza 3
Line 3 (A) - repeat of stanza 1, line 4
Line 4 (B) - new → becomes line 3 of stanza 3

[Continue pattern...]

Final Stanza:
Line 1 - repeat from previous stanza
Line 2 - line 3 from stanza 1
Line 3 - repeat from previous stanza
Line 4 - line 1 from stanza 1

name: Triolet
description: French form of 8 lines with two rhymes and two refrains. Line 1 repeats as lines 4 and 7; line 2 repeats as line 8. Usually in iambic tetrameter.
templateContent:
Line 1 (A) - first refrain
Line 2 (B) - second refrain
Line 3 (a) - rhymes with A
Line 4 (A) - repeat of line 1
Line 5 (a) - rhymes with A
Line 6 (b) - rhymes with B
Line 7 (A) - repeat of line 1
Line 8 (B) - repeat of line 2

name: Ballad
description: Narrative poem in quatrains with alternating 4-stress and 3-stress lines. Traditional form for storytelling, often with a refrain. ABAB or ABCB rhyme scheme.
templateContent:
Line 1 (A) - 8 syllables (4 stresses)
Line 2 (B) - 6 syllables (3 stresses)
Line 3 (A or C) - 8 syllables (4 stresses)
Line 4 (B) - 6 syllables (3 stresses)

[Repeat quatrain pattern for narrative]

[Optional refrain after each stanza]

name: Ottava Rima
description: Italian stanza form of 8 lines in iambic pentameter. Six lines of alternating rhyme followed by a couplet. Used by Byron in Don Juan.
templateContent:
Line 1 (A) - iambic pentameter
Line 2 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 3 (A) - iambic pentameter
Line 4 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 5 (A) - iambic pentameter
Line 6 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 7 (C) - couplet begins
Line 8 (C) - couplet ends

name: Terza Rima
description: Italian form of interlocking tercets where the middle line of each stanza rhymes with the first and third lines of the next. Ends with a single line or couplet. Used by Dante in the Divine Comedy.
templateContent:
Stanza 1:
Line 1 (A)
Line 2 (B) - links to next stanza
Line 3 (A)

Stanza 2:
Line 4 (B) - rhymes with line 2
Line 5 (C) - links to next stanza
Line 6 (B)

Stanza 3:
Line 7 (C) - rhymes with line 5
Line 8 (D) - links to next stanza
Line 9 (C)

[Continue pattern...]

Final line or couplet:
Line N (rhymes with middle line of last tercet)

name: Spenserian Stanza
description: Nine-line stanza created by Edmund Spenser for The Faerie Queene. Eight lines of iambic pentameter followed by an alexandrine (12 syllables). Interlocking rhyme scheme ABABBCBCC.
templateContent:
Line 1 (A) - iambic pentameter
Line 2 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 3 (A) - iambic pentameter
Line 4 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 5 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 6 (C) - iambic pentameter
Line 7 (B) - iambic pentameter
Line 8 (C) - iambic pentameter
Line 9 (C) - alexandrine (12 syllables)
